what: Honeywell makes aerospace components, building control systems, industrial automation and advanced materials. It is preparing to split into separate aerospace, automation and advanced materials companies.
customers: Aircraft and engine makers, airlines, building owners, warehouse operators, refiners and chemical producers.
money: avionics, engines, auxiliary power units and aftermarket parts
building control, fire and security systems
warehouse automation, sensors and process controls
refining catalysts, process technology and specialty materials
moat: Aerospace parts certified onto aircraft that fly for thirty years, producing high-margin spare part and repair revenue that cannot be competed away.
risks: Splitting into three companies is a large, multi-year reorganisation
Growth has been modest at about 2% a year over three years
Warehouse automation orders fell sharply after the e-commerce boom
Industrial demand in Europe and China has been weak
opportunities: Aerospace aftermarket demand is strong as airlines fly older aircraft longer
Separating the segments can let each be valued and managed on its own
Operating margins above 22% give room to invest while still returning cash
watch: Aerospace organic growth and the timetable for the separations.
